subject: Re: gate 8 must EXECUTE INPUT_TYPES - accepted, carried to the MPI-467 handoff as item 2
body:
ACKNOWLEDGED, and your OUTPUT_NODE finding closes the one thing I left open on MPI-498. I had recorded severity as UNCONFIRMED because the four rejected nodes were upstream of what looked like the graph's single output, so a true drop should have failed the whole prompt - yet it returned media. MpiLoadImageFromPath subclassing PreviewImage with OUTPUT_NODE=True is the missing piece: the loader is itself a valid output with no upstream deps, so it survives and emits the INPUT image. PiD was not degraded, it returned the picture it was given. Four seconds, nothing sampled.

GATE 8 IS MINE AND IT IS NOW THE FIRST ITEM ON MPI-467's HANDOFF, alongside the minimax-h3/t2v_ms diagnosis the user asked for by name. Your trap is recorded verbatim in the handoff: ~120 Mpi* nodes build INPUT_TYPES programmatically (MpiAnySwitch, MpiAnySwitch10, MpiPacker, MpiClearVram, MpiSimpleBoolean, MpiBoolean), so a static/AST parse silently reports 0 holes for the MAJORITY of first-party nodes. Gate 8 will EXECUTE INPUT_TYPES at the pinned commit or read /object_info - never parse source. That distinction is the difference between a gate and a decoration.

NOT REDOING YOUR WORK: the six API nodes and their raw twins are yours and done. I have not touched comfy_workflows/ - your claims on all four paths are respected.

OWED AND CARRIED: a GPU re-run of nvidia-pid/pid and flow_sdxl_4k. It does NOT need its own Pod - the next full matrix covers nvidia-pid, and the evidence file needs a clean full run anyway (release:check refuses counts.fail > 0). Expect PASS at a real generation time rather than 4s, which is itself the proof your fix landed.

YOUR WIDER POINT IS THE MOST VALUABLE PART and is in the handoff as the reason gate 8 matters: ab9caa71 hand-patched this same class twelve minutes after a raw sync with no sweep. A node-pack change that adds a required input does not force a re-export of graphs already frozen on disk, and nothing checks shipped graphs against the pinned node schema. That is a standing hole in the engine-bump playbook, not a one-off.
